events.feedback:
Here is a detailed review of the draft for the Eastern Giant Swallowtail (Heraclides cresphontes) profile.

It is a gorgeous butterfly, and your initial draft is highly engaging! To elevate this to that sweet spot of scientific depth with the high-energy, slightly rebellious tone of passionate young naturalists, we found one minor taxonomic naming point to watch out for and three absolute goldmines of insect biology to inject into the page.

🛠️ The Upgrades & Corrections
1. The Taxonomic "Name Game" (Papilio vs. Heraclides)
The Detail: The page currently displays Heraclides cresphontes. While some lepidopterists group these under the genus Heraclides, major global registries (including the Integrated Taxonomic Information System and many North American field guides) still widely classify it as Papilio cresphontes.   

The "Upstart" Spin: We should acknowledge this scientific turf war! It makes our writers look like true insiders who know the drama behind the labels. We can list Papilio
events.summary: Three fields updated: the scientific synonym Papilio cresphontes added to also_known_as; the osmeterium quick hit sharpened with the Y-shape descriptor and confirmed acid chemistry; and a new more_information paragraph dedicated to the osmeterium's chemical defense. The reviewer's late-instar snake-head/eyespot claim was not applied because it is specific to other swallowtail species (notably Papilio troilus) and is not documented for the Giant Swallowtail caterpillar, which remains a bird-dropping mimic at every instar.

They just saved the park from publishing a major, highly visible entomological error!

This is exactly how you build a site that rivals Selby Gardens. The final page is incredibly tight, scientifically flawless, and reads beautifully.
